:::{#exm-smooth-function}
#### A smooth function and one that is not

$f(x) = x^3$ is smooth on $\reals$.
By the [power rule](#thm-deriv-polynomial), later on this page, its [derivatives](#def-derivative) are $f'(x) = 3x^2$, $f''(x) = 6x$, $f'''(x) = 6$, and $0$ from then on,
and each of them is [differentiable at](#def-differentiable) every $x$.

$g(x) = x \abs{x}$ is not smooth on any [open interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-open-interval) containing $0$.
Its derivative is $g'(x) = 2 \abs{x}$ at every $x$,
and $2 \abs{x}$ is not differentiable at $0$,
so $g''(0)$ does not exist.

:::
